title: Cassoulet Improv
description:
This cassoulet recipe is hearty, authentic, and actually easy to make. It is reminiscent of the authentic casserole of
preserved duck, sausages and beans that is the heart & soul of Gascon cooking. Here, I’ve used things that
happened to be around in the fridge, freezer, and pantry that day. It’s still delicious. I also had some haricot verts
with some lemon juice and a simple salad of lettuce, tomato, and blue cheese. Improvise and enjoy!
ingredients: 4 or more slices of bacon, roughly cut into pieces
4 or more cloves garlic, roughly chopped
1 handful baby carrots (more if only veggie) Improv
1-2 tablespoons Italian or French spice mixture, oregano,
thyme, maybe some red pepper flakes
1-2 sausage links per person, Andouille, Kielbasa, Chicken with Spices, etc., sliced into bite-size pieces
Some leftover roasted chicken (in bite-sized pieces), or fresh thighs or legs
1 cup or so of breadcrumbs (Panko preferred, Italian flavored good)
directions: Sauté the bacon in a little olive oil for about 3 minutes (no need to be completely cooked crisp).
Take the bacon out, leaving the fats still in, and cook the onions and spices for about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for about 1 minute.
Then add the carrots, celery, bacon back in, beans (with juice), chicken broth, and sausage slices. Turn the
heat down low and let the flavors meld together.
If you’re using fresh chicken pieces, sauté them with some salt in a bit of hot olive oil for about 3 minutes
a side (just browning them up nicely).
Pour all the beans and stuff into a nice round or oval dish (“cassoulet”). If you’ve just browed chicken
pieces, add them now, and spread everything around. (If using leftover chicken, save until a little later.)
Remove from over (carefully), add leftover chicken if using. Then spread the breadcrumbs all over the top
and spray with a little olive oil.
Return to the oven and bake for another 30 minutes or so, when the breadcrumbs have browned nicely
Remove from oven carefully and eat piping hot.
